data.segment_title: Economy: Bailout Bill / House Vote / Boehner, Hoyer Interviews
data.segment_description:
(Columbus: Katie Couric)  The stunning House defeat of President Bush's administration's economic rescue plan and the resulting huge one-day drop in the stock market reported.  

(Washington: Bob Orr)  The background to the bill's defeat examined; details given about the political fingerpointing, the bailout compromise, the Democrats' demands and the conservatives' opposition to a bailout of Wall Street.  [Two REPRESENTATIVES, Representatives Carolyn MALONEY†, John CAMPBELL†- speak about the bill.]  [Speaker of the House Nancy PELOSI - criticizes the "anything goes" mentality of President Bush's administration.]  [Representatives John BOEHNER, Barney FRANK - offer differing opinions on whether Pelosi's speech is to blame {for the bill's defeat}.]  [President BUSH - comments on what's next.]  

(Columbus: Katie Couric)  Live interview held with negotiator Boehner about the financial crisis.  [BOEHNER - says the constituents oppose the bill and that the risk is so important we cannot fail to act; comments on the reaction to Pelosi's partisan speech; says Pelosi will have to make the decision on how to move ahead together.]  

(Columbus: Katie Couric)  Live interview held with Democratic Representative Steny Hoyer about the bill's failure.  [HOYER - says we Democrats did our job, but the Republican ideology overcame common sense; calls for work in a bipartisan fashion; quotes Frank on the vote to stabilize the economy.]  

(Columbus: Katie Couric)  The market meltdown on Wall Street noted.  

(New York: Anthony Mason)  The reaction of the market to the failure of the bailout bill examined; details given of the sale of Wachovia to Citigroup, the plunge in National City stock, actions in Britain and Belgium and concern about the credit markets.  [Seaport Securities Corp. Ted WEISBERG†- calls it mind-boggling.]  [Pacific Growth Equities, LLC Stephen MASSOCCA†, Moody's economy.com economist Mark ZANDI†- explain that something needs to get done to get relief to the credit system.]  A list of companies in danger of defaulting outlined on screen.  

(Columbus: Katie Couric)  The agreement by the two presidential candidates that Congress must pass a financial bailout noted.  [Senator Barack OBAMA - offer views on Congress, the economy and an emergency package.]  [Senator John McCAIN - says it is time to fix the problem.]  

(Columbus: Katie Couric)  The view of the people in Columbus, Ohio, presented.  [Four RESIDENTS - talk about the economy, politics and the bailout.]  

(Columbus: Katie Couric)  Report introduced.  

(Los Angeles: Sandra Hughes)  The financial temperature across the country presented.  [Los Angeles residents Kevin SCHINI†, Carol BAILEY, Ralph DAVIS†, Scott GREENBERG†; in Elmhurst, Illinois, resident David BERKSHIRE†; Chicago resident Tracy WOZNIAKOWSKI†; Miami resident Bobby OXENHOREN†- comment on the economy and their own fiancees.]

Katie Couric Reports (Campaign 2008: McCain and Palin Interview)
data.segment_description: (Columbus: Katie Couric)  Today's joint interview held with Senator John McCain and running mate Governor Sarah Palin.  [PALIN - comments on what America should be doing in Pakistan and her response to a hollered question this weekend about Pakistan; asserts she is ready to serve as vice president with her executive experience.]  [McCAIN - comments on Palin getting caught by "gotcha journalism"; recalls the early views of Ronald Reagan and Bill Clinton before they became presidents; notes the excitement brought by Palin.]   (Columbus: Katie Couric)  Tomorrow's interview on the campaign trail with Palin previewed.
